subject: Physics
title: Physics - Form 2 NECTA Pilot (2025) Paper 11
instructions: This paper consists of sections A, B and C with a total of ten (10) questions.
Answer all questions in the spaces provided.
Section A and C carries fifteen (15) marks each and section B carries seventy (70) marks.
All writing must be in blue or black ink.
Communication devices and unauthorised materials are not allowed in the assessment room.
Calculators and mathematical tables may be used in the assessment room.
Write your Assessment Number at the top right corner of every page.
The following information may be useful: (i) Acceleration due to gravity, g = 10 m/s-2. (ii) Pie π = 3.14

sections.name: Section A
sections.instructions: Answer all questions in this section.

questions.text: For each of the items (i) - (x), choose the correct answer from the given alternatives and write its letter in the box provided. (10 marks)

items.text: A student lifts a load and measures height using a meter rule. What physical quantity does the student calculate?
Why does a plastic comb rubbed with dry hair attracts small pieces of paper?

options.B: Because the comb gains electric charge

items.text: Which devices can be used to demonstrate the existence of atmospheric pressure?
Explain wind as a source of energy
What is the SI unit of linear momentum?
What is the origin of magnetism?
If one bulb in a series circuit is removed, what will happen to other bulbs?

questions.text: Match the functions of instruments in List A with their corresponding instruments in List B by writing the correct answer below the item number in the table provided. (5 marks)
ListA: Measures the gas pressure in a car tyres.
Used to free blocked water sinks.
Used for sucking and ejecting liquid by increasing and decreasing pressure.
Allows water to flow because of pressure differences.

sections.name: Section B
sections.instructions: Answer all questions in this section.

questions.stem: Measurement: beaker contains 120 cm3 liquid, pipette 25 cm3 used thrice.

sub_questions.label: b
sub_questions.text: Calculate volume left in original beaker.

questions.stem: Explain Newton's laws and conservation of momentum.

sub_questions.label: a
sub_questions.text: State Newton's second law and define linear momentum.

sub_questions.label: b
sub_questions.text: Distinguish elastic vs inelastic collisions with example.

questions.stem: A man mass 40 kg walks up 25 steps each 20 cm high in 10 s. Find power.
Explain simple machines - lever and pulley.

sub_questions.label: a
sub_questions.text: Determine mechanical advantage of lever (load 60N effort 20N).

sub_questions.label: b
sub_questions.text: Explain pulley system velocity ratio and efficiency.

questions.stem: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s2 for 5 seconds.

sub_questions.label: b
sub_questions.text: Explain whether motion would still be uniformly accelerated if acceleration changed midway.

questions.stem: A plastic rod is rubbed with a dry cloth and attracts small pieces of paper.

sub_questions.label: a
sub_questions.text: Apply concept of electron transfer to explain how rod becomes charged.

sub_questions.label: b
sub_questions.text: Why can rod attract neutral pieces? What happens in humid environment?

questions.stem: Two students designed circuits with three 6 Ohm resistors to 12V battery: A series, B parallel.

sub_questions.label: b
sub_questions.text: Calculate current drawn in each case.

sub_questions.label: c
sub_questions.text: Show which arrangement is safer for 2A rated battery.

questions.stem: Two students designed circuits using three identical resistors each of 6 Ohm connected to 12 V battery. Student A connects them in series and student B connects them in parallel.

sub_questions.label: a
sub_questions.text: Calculate total resistance for each arrangement.

sub_questions.label: b
sub_questions.text: Calculate the current drawn from battery in each case.

sub_questions.label: c
sub_questions.text: Using mathematical evidence, show arrangement safer for 2A rated battery.
